claims.summary: The Djinn costs four mana; one Ritual from one Swamp yields three. Its damage occurs only on its controller’s upkeep. The new scene pays with Ritual plus a separate Swamp.
Rosewater recalled initial skepticism about the self-damage before players recognized the efficient body.
Andrew Raichlin won the twelve-player October 11, 2015 Card and Board event with the published black-white list.
Taiga both casts the red Ape and satisfies its Forest condition, making it 2/3; mentioning Forest does not change red Commander color identity.
The official 1994 Worlds retrospective publishes Lestree’s Ape list and documents his runner-up finish.
In 2003 Rosewater acknowledged that banning Kird Ape at the start of Extended had been a mistake; the article no longer invents a policy rationale.
A turn-one 2/1 without haste can deal eight damage by the end of turn five, not ten.
Official retrospective confirms Chanpheng’s 1996 championship and the uncastable Sleight of Mind caused by the omitted blue sources.
Silvestri’s December 6, 2006 composite is not a tournament registration. The three named fetchland quantities are explicit editorial completions of ten unspecified source slots.
The Djinn triggers during its controller’s upkeep. Granted forestwalk remains after Armageddon, but does not prevent blocking if the defender has no Forest. Factory also dies to Armageddon.
Official results place Lestrée second and Poulter fourth in February 1996; the final paired Erhnamgeddon against Loconto’s control deck.
Tapping City during a cast puts its damage trigger above that spell; tapping it first allows an instant response to resolve above the damage.
Flores’s published Weissman version contains three Cities, rather than establishing a universal four-copy count.
The organizer’s 2015 U/R list contains the City, Volcanic Island, Bolt, Strip Mine and Mountain used in the two reconstructed scenes.
Exactly seven cards are required on activation; a later hand-size change does not invalidate an announced activation. A cantrip normally preserves final hand size.
Arena announced its digital Special Guests Library for Timeless; the April 20 announcement documents the Historic pre-ban.
Library is restricted in Vintage and banned in Legacy and Commander on the official list checked October 16, 2026.
The Japanese official August 19, 2018 Survival registration contains Bazaar, Rootwalla, Squee, Vengevine and Hollow One.
Madness waits for the activation to finish; Rootwalla and Hollow One can be the first and second creature spells, returning haste Vengevine. Alternative-cost spells still receive applicable taxes.
Bazaar is unrestricted in Vintage and banned in Legacy on the official list checked October 16, 2026.
Workshop mana pays only for artifact spells, including their casting taxes. It cannot pay for Welder or Factory activation. The story uses three Lotus mana for the taxed Welder.
The Wire’s controller can order fading to resolve before the tap trigger. An opponent with fewer eligible untapped permanents taps only those available.
Wizards restricted Chalice in 2015 and explained the problem with consistent turn-one suppression of zero-mana artifacts.
Jason Carl’s December 3, 1997 DCI announcement adds Strip Mine to the Classic Type I restricted list effective January 1, 1998.
Contemporary July 2004 rules advice confirms that Crucible does not grant additional land plays.
Strip Mine can target a basic Forest. The speaker being on the play leaves the turn-one Elf unable to tap during speaker turn two; tapping and sacrificing the Mine is the activation cost.
Modern Horizons 2 notes explicitly permit animating an older Factory, blocking, and then tapping it to become 3/3; a newly controlled animated Factory cannot attack or use its tap abilities.
Rosewater explains that Foundry’s attacking-only pump restrains the defensive 3/3 available to Factory.
Galli’s February 21, 2026 Premodern sheet has four Factories, three Standstills and two Faerie Conclaves; no placement is claimed.

method: Source pages inspected in this session. Documentary registrations and rules are distinct from reconstructed table stories.
